_note: Place visits: the Rhondda and Bethesda and Dyffryn Ogwen.
common.back_note: If you leave without choosing, nothing is lost. Any card of yours at work here works as normal, but no better.
common.tests_note: The future is never certain, so each test is tried many times. A test passes if it works about 6 times in 10.
common.none_yet: No picks yet. You can make up to {n}.
rhondda.history: From the 1850s two narrow valleys filled with pits and terraces. Coal output peaked around 1913. The last Rhondda pit closed in 1990. The tips stayed: heaps of coal waste, called spoil, on the hillsides.
rhondda.tip_source_bgs: A landslide record on or near a tip (British Geological Survey)
rhondda.tip_source_osm: The outline of a heap of coal waste (OpenStreetMap)
rhondda.risk_raised: The risk is higher this decade: {trend}.
rhondda.wimd: {name}: number {rank} of {areas} small neighbourhoods in Wales, where 1 is the poorest. From the {edition} deprivation index, which the tip map uses. Figures elsewhere use the 2025 index.
rhondda.wimd_deprived: in the poorest tenth of Wales
rhondda.buildings_note: Building outlines from OpenStreetMap. Some are missing.
rhondda.rule_sentence: Below means within {d} m of the tip and at least {h} m lower than its base.
rhondda.rule_slider: How far counts as below, in metres
rhondda.rule_note: A rough guide, not an engineer’s check. Change the distance and the counts change.
rhondda.rule_register: The official list of old coal tips is not open data. So it is not used here.
rhondda.tests.exposure: Did you protect enough homes? Your picks must cover enough of the homes below the tips. Risky tips count for more.
rhondda.tests.fairness: Did you help the poorest streets? At least one pick must sit above a neighbourhood in the poorest tenth of Wales.
rhondda.tests.lifelines: Are the schools and the railway safe? No high-risk tip may be left above a school or the railway.
bethesda.prompt: Three picks to tie the quarry to the valley.
bethesda.dilemma: Visitors have come to the quarry. Will young people here get homes, jobs and Welsh-speaking streets from it? Or will it all pass them by?
bethesda.history: Penrhyn quarry was once the biggest slate quarry in the world. A lockout from 1900 to 1903 split the valley. The slate landscape became a World Heritage Site in 2021.
bethesda.half_without: Half as strong unless you have played {card}.
bethesda.river_flips: Hurts the river in dry summers.
bethesda.tests.aros: Can young people stay? You need a homes pick and a work pick that both work.
bethesda.tests.iaith: Is Welsh still heard on the street? Your picks must help Welsh enough to stop it falling.
bethesda.tests.pwysau: Can the valley cope? Visitors, lorries and the river must not be too much for it.
bethesda.facts_note: Facts say “to check” until a source is confirmed.
rhondda.prompt.one: The money covers 1 tip this turn. There are more tips than money.
rhondda.prompt.other: The money covers {n} tips this turn. There are more tips than money.
bethesda.about: The place, and what it will check
